name: Teamtailor
tagline: Applicant tracking system with a hosted careers site, candidate pipelines and hiring team collaboration.

pricing.basis: quote based, scales with company size
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The mechanical core of an ATS is unglamorous CRUD: a public job page, an application form with a file upload, a kanban of stages, notes and templated emails. An agent will give you that in a session and it will genuinely work if you are hiring for one small team. What it will not give you is the part companies actually buy: syndication to Indeed, LinkedIn and local job boards, calendar-synced interview scheduling, structured scorecards everyone adopts, and GDPR retention and consent handling that survives a Spanish or Swedish data request. Teamtailor also sells the candidate-facing polish, the careers page that makes a 12-person company look like a real employer, which is a design problem more than a code problem. Build it if you want a private pipeline tracker, buy it if hiring is a recurring business process with multiple interviewers.
coreLoopDIY: Self-hosted job board plus application form that files candidates into a drag-and-drop stage pipeline with notes and templated email replies.
requirements: A small server or VPS to host the public careers page
Somewhere to store CV uploads, local disk or S3-compatible bucket
Someone willing to handle data deletion requests by hand
whatYouLose: Multiposting to job boards and aggregators, so nobody finds your openings
Interview scheduling that talks to real calendars and handles timezones
Built-in GDPR consent, retention timers and candidate data export
A careers page designed by people who do this full time
Permissions, audit trails and anything resembling hiring team etiquette
moatNotes: Job board syndication is the quiet moat: dozens of per-board contracts and feed formats you cannot negotiate as one person.
whyPeopleStillPay: Hiring is bursty and high-stakes, and the cost of a lost candidate is far higher than a software subscription. Recruiters do not want to debug a file upload while a shortlist goes cold, and legal does not want candidate CVs sitting in a folder on someone's VPS with no retention policy. Teamtailor sells the whole surface: the careers site, the distribution, the scheduling, the audit trail, and the fact that every interviewer can log in and leave feedback without being taught a tool. A personal build covers the tracking and none of the reach.
notes: The pipeline is a weekend; the pipeline being full is not.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted applicant tracking system for a small team. Single stack, no menus.

Stack: Next.js (App Router, TypeScript), SQLite via Prisma, Tailwind for styling, Nodemailer for email. Everything runs locally with `npm run dev` and deploys as one Node process. No external SaaS, no analytics, no telemetry.

Data model:
- Job: title, department, location, employmentType, descriptionMarkdown, status (draft | open | closed), publicSlug
- Candidate: name, email, phone, cvFilePath, coverLetter, source, jobId, stage, createdAt
- Stage: ordered per job, default set Applied, Screening, Interview, Offer, Hired, Rejected
- Note: candidateId, author, body, createdAt
- EmailTemplate: name, subject, bodyMarkdown with {{name}} and {{job}} placeholders

Public side (no auth):
- /jobs lists open jobs, /jobs/[publicSlug] renders the job description and an application form
- Form takes name, email, phone, cover letter and a PDF or DOCX upload, max 10MB, stored under ./uploads with a generated filename
- On submit, create the Candidate in the Applied stage and send an acknowledgement email using the template named "acknowledgement"

Admin side (single shared password from ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env, cookie session, that is enough):
- /admin/jobs CRUD for jobs
- /admin/pipeline/[jobId]: kanban board of stages, drag and drop candidates between stages with optimistic UI
- Candidate drawer: contact details, CV download link, notes thread, and a "send email" action that picks a template, previews the rendered text and sends via SMTP
- /admin/templates CRUD for email templates
- CSV export of candidates per job

Secrets in .env.example: ADMIN_PASSWORD, SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS, MAIL_FROM.

Explicitly out of scope: job board syndication, LinkedIn or Indeed feeds, calendar integration, interview scheduling, multi-user accounts and permissions, SSO, structured scorecards, GDPR retention automation, mobile apps.

Include a seed script with two jobs, five fake candidates and the acknowledgement template, plus a README covering setup, where uploads live and how to back up the SQLite file.
